lines.en: : Twenty-three!
: What?
: It’s where we are!
: I figured it out!
: How long have I been here?
: I knew it wasn’t twenty-two because twenty-two is gone. And twenty-four is wrong, so twenty-three is right! I did a good job!
: Yasu, how long have I been here?
: Since all of this began.
: I don’t mean at the party. I mean right here in front of you. When did I get here and where was I beforehand?
: If you’re going to use your inexplicable brain powers for anything, use them to help me right now because I need it.
: You’ve been right in front of me all along. It’s just that you’ve been everywhere else as well and I’m too focused on Him to keep track of your every move.
: But He is sleepy now. And His season has come to an end.
: Summer isn’t over yet. Everything still feels wrong. It’s supposed to go back to normal when the seasons change. I’m supposed to be fixed.
: I’m afraid that isn’t possible anymore.
: Unless you’re willing to destroy yourself and rebuild from the ground up.

: The whispers of the world have turned to laughter. And they aim their jokes at you — the one they call the child of makeshift deities. But it is in complete disregard of the fact that there is but one deity.
: Then...
: Then come with me. I’ll give you my “light.” I’ll take something that doesn’t belong to me.
: Oh...you poor, little lamb.
: Your light’s already burnt out.
: You have nothing I want or need anymore.
: But when the world shifts again and His power dawns once more, you will be reassessed! And then, if you pass all of His tests, your light could come back. Doesn’t that sound wonderful?
: Yasu...what is happening to me?
: You’ve been a bad boy.
: You broke too many rules when all you had to do was spread yourself out.
: Now, like a plague, it will be your misery that swarms the land in place of your seed.
: And all of us are doomed to crumble beneath you as you fall and you flail and forget who you are.
: Was it worth it in the end?
: Did you have a good time?
: Did you make some happy memories?
: If you did, then write them down.
: Look back on them years from now, long after your mind has been purged of the darkness you’ve invited in.
: Look back on them and remember...so you won’t make the same mistakes again.
: May I act as your shepherd one last time, Svarog? Before the party ends and all of our doubts are washed away by the rain?
: Can I? Please?
: Do whatever you want, Yasu...
: I don’t get it anymore.
: Then leave everything to those who do.
: For even the most lost, unfortunate souls will one day find their way back to Him. And I trust that you will accept this in your heart when the rest of your options have expired.
: We live in a beautiful world — even if it is so often polluted by those who don’t understand.
: But you don’t need to understand to make your time here feel good. And if you know there’s not much left, why let the fear of the unknown spoil what remains?
: If I were you, I would enjoy my final moments.
: I would spend them with the people I cherish.
: And you don’t realize how lucky you are to have so many of them.
: Was it worth it in the end?
: Did you have a good time?
: And did you make some happy memories?
: Ah! There she is.
: Because I did.
: And it would be nice if you did too.
: I swear, letting you into the manga club was like taking on a permanent escort quest. And one that never ends at that. How do you keep disappearing without anyone even noticing?
: It helps that I’m an insignificant husk of a girl who no one would mind chopping into pieces and adding to a hot pot.
: What a strangely specific form of self-deprecation.
: You have been gone for quite a while, Harold.
: Herald, Kafka. Herald.
: Harold Shipman of Bestwood Estate, husband to Primrose Oxtoby and licensed general practitioner.
: Did you and Yasu have a secret meeting where you just decided to become creative all of a sudden? What in the bloody hell is going on right now?
: You weren’t looking for me, were you?
: If I say that I was, will you assume it means that I have fallen in love with you? Because the mere thought of that makes me want to swallow fire.
: She’s obviously kidding, Sir. Kafka’s costume is just a little too tight in certain areas and it’s causing her to act a bit-
: Hey, sorry to interrupt, but have any of you guys seen Io around here? She kind of just...disappeared without saying anything.
: Ahh, yes. The Irish goodbye. Or, as they call it where I come from — goodbye.
: Is disappearing without saying anything unusual for her? I had assumed that was simply how she operated.
: She normally says something to me at least. And she’s not answering her phone either.
: Svarog knows where she is.
: Who? Svarog? Is that another one of Ayane’s butlers or something?
: Is what Clara says true, Sir? Do you know what happened to the not-so-friendly neighborhood Lawson employee?
: Wait, Yasu was talking about you, Sensei? Why didn’t you say anything?
: Because I have no idea what happened to her. One second I was talking to her, and the next she was gone.
: Well...do you know which direction she went in? Because, I’m probably just overreacting right now, but I can’t help but feel a little worried.
: I have no idea. Sorry.
: Ugh. Gosh darn it. Guess I’ll just try calling the bath house or something.
: While she does that, want to check out some of the stuff I brought you from my stash? I’ve already made sure to screen it for inappropriate content and you’re good to go!
: Hooray! More pictures!
: And for you, Kafka, I’ve uncovered a relatively rare cooking series that I’m quite sure you’ll come to-
: I will rendezvous with you shortly, Ginger Wolf. I have a matter to take care of with Svarog first.
: A side quest? Right now? But we’re already partied up.
: Tsuneyo Tojo has left the group.
: Kafka?! Tsuneyo?! Where did you go?!
: Aaaaaaaaah!
: That should take care of them for a while. Do you have a minute to spare, Sensei? I have something I’d like to ask you.
: If it’s about what happened in the infirmary, it wasn’t me who-
: I have no idea what this is about an infirmary. You just said something earlier that piqued my interest and I have been unsure of how to approach you in regard to it ever since.
: You’re going to have to refresh my memory then, because I have no clue what you’re talking about.
: The ferris wheel.
: Why do I have memories of such a thing when we’ve never done something like that before?
: Because we have.
: When? And why do you remember this trip, but I do not? And note that I will not hesitate to cut you down if I discover you drugged or used memory-manipulating magic on me.
: I didn’t do anything. It’s the world that used “memory magic” or whatever you want to call it. I wanted you to keep that memory.
: I see.

: What do you mean, “I see?” What part of that can you possibly see? It doesn’t make any sense and you should be accusing me of fucking with you right now for even attempting to use that as an explanation.
: Perhaps you have just fucked me so many times by now that I have grown used to it? I do not know.
: But I can sense you are telling the truth. And the idea that my memories are being somehow altered helps explain why I’ve felt rather unusual as of late.
: Unusual how?
: As in my heart starts beating faster whenever you’re nearby.
: It’s rather annoying, actually. So if you know how to make that stop, I would greatly appreciate it.
: Sensei?
: I have no idea how to help with that, Tsuneyo.
: But I’m sure it will go away on its own.
: I see.
: Then, are there any concerns you would like to raise to me as well? It is only fair that I address at least one of them as that would account for an equal exchange of emotions between us.
: Tsuneyo...
: Am I a better person now than I was when you met me?
: I am, right?
: Like, don’t get me wrong, I’m still horrible. And I have a million miles to go before I’m worth wasting any amount of words on, but...
: I’m changing for the better, aren’t I? This isn’t all for nothing. I’m starting to do the right thing and...it’s taking me a while to get there, but...I will.
: It would be a waste to send me back now, wouldn’t it?
: Back to where, Sensei?
: To...nowhere.

: I don’t really know, to be honest. But you’re not the only one feeling “unusual” right now. It’s just that for me, it’s consuming and replacing every thought I try to think with the idea that this could be the end.
: That I could be the one to wake up tomorrow with my memories all fucked up instead of any of you.
: Correct me if I’m wrong, but weren’t your memories already “fucked up” to begin with? I’ve heard that time and time again in regard to your past, but I’m not quite sure of the details.
: Yeah...they are. Or were. But they’re starting to come back. There are people who are helping me get them back.
: Then who’s to say those people won’t be there to help you again should you get “fucked up” even more?
: Am I using that term correctly? “Fucked up?” That is not sexual in nature as well, is it?
: No, you’re using it correctly. And thank you.
: Let’s ride the ferris wheel again if I wake up in my own body tomorrow.
: Sensei...
: Absolutely not.
: Wha-
: Hey! Are you ready?
: Ayane? Ready for what?
: The afterparty thing we talked about earlier. We’re heading over to our usual karaoke place to end the night with a bang.
: Don’t say it like that. He’ll get ideas.
: I call shotgun.
: We’re just leaving in the middle of the party? We’re not even going to try to sneak away or anything?
: There’s not really any point when things are already starting to wind down. You’re still coming, right?
: I mean...yeah. I can come. But, fair warning, I’m still not feeling like my “normal” self.
: That’s fine. I’m kinda tired too. And, if worse comes to worst, you can use my thighs as a pillow and relax while the rest of us sing. As long as you don’t pretend they’re Maya’s, I mean.
In the midst of all this mental chaos, there was one piece of advice that managed to lure me in.
And strangely enough, it came from Yasu of all people.
If this really is the end...and I never make it back to the rooftop...I should spend my final moments with those I cherish, shouldn’t I?
The girls who stand before me are my everything.
They’re the first ones I laid these brand new eyes on and...I’d be happy if they’re the last as well.
Besides, there’s still a chance that all those fatalistic thoughts within me spawning like maggots in hot trash are all just...nonsense, right? That I’m making them up?
This is the final hurdle.
It’s those most terrible, unspoken urges I have to overcome and conquer if I ever want to become a better me, right?
That’s all this is. It’s one more hurdle.
It’s one more chance for me to be a good boy.
And if I can hold out for one more night, they’ll all go away.
Everything will go away.
And I’ll be free to live the happy...quiet life I’ve always wanted.
: Hey...
But could never possibly deserve.
: Are we...getting ready to leave?
: Oh, hey. Are you feeling better? I was actually just about to come see if you were still up for the trip.
: Yeah...I’m okay now...
: I just needed...a little rest...that’s all...
: Great! I guess we’re all set, then. Anyone want to go say their final goodbyes, or are we all going to follow in Io’s footsteps and vanish without saying anything?
: Goodbye.
: Is it just me or was that somehow even worse than leaving without saying anything?
: Is it really okay for you to...leave while everyone else is still here?
: It’ll be fine. There’s nothing Geoffrey can’t handle.
: What matters most is just getting Sensei out of here undetected before one of the other girls-
: Run!
Before I’m able to react, Ami grabs my hand and sprints toward the exit.
And, of course, the entire room takes notice.
But, right now...
I don’t care.
I don’t care about anything.
